sources.source_name: American Olean Product Specifications — Ceramic Floor Tile
sources.snippet: Theoretical Bold: standard residential ceramic floor tile. White body construction with digital inkjet glaze surface. PEI Class 3 (light-to-moderate residential traffic). Water absorption 0.5-3% (vitreous range — classified as ceramic, not porcelain). Calibrated sizing (sorted by dimension groups), not fully rectified on all lines. DCOF ≥0.42 on textured finishes. Available in standard formats (12x12, 12x24). Limited lifetime residential warranty from Mohawk Industries.
sources.classification_reason: Manufacturer specifications with ANSI standards compliance.

sources.source_name: American Olean Heritage — Oldest US Ceramic Brand
sources.snippet: American Olean: founded 1923 in Lansdale, Pennsylvania. One of the oldest ceramic tile brands in the United States. Now owned by Mohawk Industries (NYSE: MHK) through Dal-Tile Corporation. Shares parent company with Daltile and Marazzi USA. Positioned as a value tier below Daltile within Mohawk portfolio — same parent manufacturing infrastructure, different product positioning and quality tier.

sources.source_name: r/Tile — American Olean vs Daltile Platform Comparison
sources.snippet: American Olean and Daltile come from the same company (Mohawk). AO is positioned below Daltile in quality and design sophistication. It's perfectly fine ceramic for residential use — bathrooms, backsplash, light-traffic floors. The ceramic body is standard white body, water absorption is in the vitreous range (not porcelain). I wouldn't put it in a heavy-traffic entryway, but for a bathroom it's a solid, reliable product with Mohawk warranty behind it.
sources.classification_reason: Professional installer with platform comparison knowledge.

sources.snippet: Standard residential ceramic tile (vitreous class, water absorption 0.5-3%) is appropriate for interior floors and walls in residential settings with light to moderate traffic. Not recommended for exterior or freeze-thaw environments. Installation requires polymer-modified thinset for reliable bond. Calibrated but non-rectified tiles require minimum 3/16" grout lines per TCNA recommendations.
sources.classification_reason: NTCA professional installation standards for ceramic tile class.

sources.source_name: Houzz — American Olean for Residential Use
sources.snippet: American Olean is a perfectly respectable residential tile. It's not going to wow anyone with design sophistication, but it's consistently made, the warranty is solid (Mohawk), and for a standard bathroom or laundry room it does the job. It's the 'Toyota Camry' of ceramic tile — not exciting, but reliable and affordable. I use Daltile for premium and AO for standard residential.
sources.classification_reason: Professional designer with clear brand hierarchy placement.

bottom_line: American Olean Theoretical Bold is the ceramic benchmark — 'good enough for a quality residential installation' without being premium. White body ceramic, PEI 3, vitreous water absorption (0.5-3%), calibrated but not fully rectified. Mohawk Industries ownership provides lifetime warranty and consistent manufacturing infrastructure. Professional consensus: reliable, affordable, Mohawk-backed, but positioned below Daltile in both quality and design. Suitable for bathrooms, backsplashes, and light-traffic interior floors. Not appropriate for heavy-traffic, exterior, or freeze-thaw applications.
